issues.title: DSi Manager allows installing DSiWare beyond the DSi logical storage limit
issues.body:
* **Device model:** 　AYN Thor
* **Android version:** 　13

### Description

I found what appears to be a storage limit issue with the DSi Manager.

The DSi Manager allows installing additional DSiWare titles even after the DSi logical storage limit has likely been exceeded.

The installation completes successfully, but after returning to the DSi HOME Menu, the HOME Menu fails to boot and only shows the generic DSi error screen.

If enough DSiWare titles are removed to reduce the used storage, the HOME Menu boots normally again.

### Expected behavior

The DSi Manager should prevent installing additional DSiWare once the DSiWare storage limit is reached, similar to how a real DSi behaves.

### Actual behavior

Installation succeeds, but the DSi HOME Menu becomes unusable until enough titles are removed.

### Reproduction

1. Install many DSiWare titles using DSi Manager.
2. Continue until the total used storage is close to or exceeds the DSiWare storage limit.
3. Return to the DSi HOME Menu.
4. The HOME Menu displays the generic error screen instead of booting.

### Additional information

I tested this using a USA DSi NAND because it includes Data Management.

With 15 installed DSiWare titles, only about 20 blocks of free space remained.

Since the DSi internal storage limit for DSiWare is 1024 blocks, I suspect that installing one more average-sized title exceeded this limit.

This would explain why the installation itself succeeds, but the DSi HOME Menu later fails.

It seems possible that the DSi Manager checks the physical NAND free space instead of the DSiWare logical storage limit.

issues.title: The issue was with the SAK path!! Once that’s fixed, Frontend works well up to Android 15.
issues.body:
Hi!
I’ve mentioned this issue several times, and it turns out it wasn’t a permission problem. The frontend was passing the SAF path, but MelonDS wasn’t able to receive it properly.

https://gall.dcinside.com/mgallery/board/view/?id=retrogame&no=80295&page=1#focus_cmt

There’s a user named Ssanghwacha who made a modified version of the app.

They adjusted it so that the SAF path sdcard:\a.rom — originally content://com.android.externalstorage... — is ignored, and the app directly accesses a.rom instead.
